To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the corporate governance practices of Nigerian banks are influenced by a combination of factors.

the corporate governance practices of the banks are not in line with the requirements of the Nigerian Code of Corporate Governance, which has been adopted by the banks, and that the corporate governance of Nigerian banks is affected by human actions, a lack of leadership and the influence of culture.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the corporate governance practices of banks in the Nigerian banking industry.
the nature of the relationship between corporate governance and the culture and leadership of banks in Nigeria.
the corporate governance practices of banks in Nigeria.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
corporate governance in the Nigerian banking industry is affected by human actions (i.e., human actions and inactions, and lack of leadership), and this is the core of the substantive theory.

the corporate governance practices in Nigerian banks are influenced by the nature of human action and the absence of leadership, and that this is the result of a lack of cooperation and trust among the stakeholders.
the theory of corporate governance in the Nigerian context is a function of culture and leadership and is influenced by the social contract, trust and cooperation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed a theory of corporate governance in banks in Nigeria that explains why banks have failed to implement good corporate governance practices.
we have been able to show that the corporate governance of Nigerian banks is affected by human actions (such as greed) and a lack of effective leadership.
it is an attempt to explore the phenomena of corporate governance of banks, the factors influencing it and the outcomes of these influences.
The main takeaway from our work is that
corporate governance is not a static concept.
corporate governance is not just about compliance with rules and regulation, it is about the culture and leadership of an organization, and how it affects the behavior of its employees.
, while there may be no silver bullet for corporate governance, the social contract strategy is a promising approach that can help to address the free-rider issues in corporate governance.
